data.question_intent: Quantify Hong Kong banking NII and discuss hedging policy impact on rate sensitivity over three years.
data.question_quote: Just staying on NII to start with, on the $41 billion, Georges, how much of the $41 billion would relate to Hong Kong banking NII, that we understand from your messaging is maybe slightly more challenging to hedge, the more difficult to hedge part of the $41 billion?
data.answer_quote: We do reported NII by legal entity. I'm not sure if you can work it out, but Asia for us is about half, and Hong Kong is between half and two thirds of Asia. That kind of gives you a quantum of the overall component of Hong Kong. So on Hong Kong, you have the full-year NII of just under $10 billion, and then we've said that about 60% of the funding cost of the trading book is in Asia. So that's $4 billion, $5 billion, basically. It's Asia, so Hong Kong will be two-thirds of Asia, if you want. You can get to that.
data.reason: The answer provides a partial response to the question, quantifying Hong Kong NII but not addressing the full scope of the question, including the hedging policy impact on rate sensitivity over three years.
